long_biography.plain_text:
Fininvest gave Silvio Berlusconi an operating structure for reshaping Italian commercial television. He acquired Telemilano, expanded it from regional broadcasting, and joined sixteen broadcasters in a nationwide programming system under the Canale 5 name. Reteitalia supplied programmes, while Publitalia '80 sold advertising, linking content, distribution and revenue inside the same group.

The television business expanded abroad before its core interests were organised as Mediaset and listed in 1996. Berlusconi retained control through Fininvest even after stepping away from executive posts. Following his death in 2023, his five children inherited the holding, with Marina and Pier Silvio jointly assuming indirect control. That succession preserved the family ownership of the broadcasting platform he built.

Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] AC Milan: Berlusconi owned and led AC Milan through Fininvest for 31 years, during which the club won major domestic, European and world titles. [2] AC Monza: Fininvest acquired AC Monza under Berlusconi, and the club rose from Serie C to Serie A during his lifetime. [3] Advertising: Publitalia '80 made advertising sales a central revenue component of Berlusconi's integrated commercial-television model. [4] Banca Mediolanum: Berlusconi co-founded Mediolanum with Ennio Doris and retained it as a durable banking and financial-services interest within Fininvest. [5] Bank founder: Berlusconi co-founded Mediolanum with Ennio Doris and incorporated the financial-services business into Fininvest's diversified holdings. [6] Berlusconi family: Berlusconi's five children inherited the family fortune, with Marina and Pier Silvio jointly assuming indirect control of the founder-built Fininvest group. [7] Canale 5: Berlusconi transformed Telemilano into Canale 5 and used it as the core of his nationwide commercial-television system. [8] Family-controlled public company: Berlusconi retained family control of the listed Mediaset platform through Fininvest, with control passing to his children after his death. [9] Fininvest: Berlusconi founded and controlled Fininvest as the holding and operating structure joining his television, publishing, advertising, banking and sports interests. [10] Forza Italia: Berlusconi founded Forza Italia from scratch in 1994 and led it as the principal organisation of his political career. [11] Magazine publishing: Mondadori's magazine operations formed a durable part of the publishing group that Berlusconi controlled through Fininvest. [12] Media executive: Berlusconi created and directed the operating system that joined television networks, programme acquisition and advertising sales inside Fininvest. [13] Mediaset: The television networks Berlusconi assembled were organised into Mediaset, the listed broadcasting platform now known as MFE-MEDIAFOREUROPE. [14] Mondadori Group: Berlusconi acquired control of Mondadori through Fininvest, making the publisher a major and enduring part of his media group. [15] Political party founder: Berlusconi created Forza Italia from scratch and used the new party to win national office within months. [16] Political party leader: Berlusconi founded and led Forza Italia as the principal vehicle for his national political career. [17] Politician: Berlusconi founded a national political party, led multiple election campaigns and held Italian and European parliamentary office across nearly three decades. [18] Post-founder succession governance: After Berlusconi's death, Marina and Pier Silvio jointly assumed indirect control of Fininvest, preserving family governance of the founder-built group. [19] Publishing: Berlusconi expanded Fininvest into publishing by acquiring control of Mondadori and holding interests across books, magazines and newspapers. [20] Publitalia '80: Berlusconi established Publitalia '80 as the advertising-sales arm that monetised Fininvest's integrated television network. [21] Retail banking: Banca Mediolanum became a lasting consumer-banking interest within the Fininvest group Berlusconi assembled. [22] Serial entrepreneurship: Berlusconi successively founded a property developer, the Fininvest media group, a financial-services venture and a national political party. [23] Vertically integrated media: Fininvest joined programme acquisition, broadcast distribution and advertising sales through Reteitalia, its networks and Publitalia '80, creating a distinctive integrated operating model.
